facts.statement: The study examined the function of the deubiquitinase STUB1 in postoperative cognitive dysfunction.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Removing STUB1 specifically in microglia reduced cognitive deficits in mice with postoperative cognitive dysfunction.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: STUB1 targets the protein NQO1, removing ubiquitin from it to trigger its breakdown via autophagy, which promotes ferroptosis in microglia.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: STUB1 removes ubiquitin from NQO1 at the K61 site, leading to p62-mediated autophagic degradation of NQO1 and subsequent ferroptosis.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: STUB1 was not directly linked to standard ferroptosis markers like GPX4 and Nrf2, but was associated with the non-canonical signal NQO1.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: NQO1 levels were clearly associated with cognitive impairment in postoperative cognitive dysfunction.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Cell experiments showed that STUB1 promotes microglial ferroptosis in a way that depends on NQO1.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The STUB1-NQO1 pathway regulates microglial ferroptosis in postoperative cognitive dysfunction, suggesting STUB1 could be a new therapeutic target.
facts.subject: animals
